message: When an open tooltip is moved in the DOM and its cs-hide is cancelled, the new `this.open = true` keeps it on screen but skips the show branch, so its Escape listener and dismissible registration are never restored.
No test checks Escape or dismissible registration after a cancelled hide, the reconnect path, or a cancelled hide through the public hide() method.
The connectedCallback re-open hack toggles open to fire public, cancelable cs-hide/cs-show events just to re-register listeners, and it is the root cause of raw finding 1.

Setting this.open = true inside the open watcher flips open false then true, which likely re-runs handleOpenChange and dispatches a second cs-show (and replays the show animation) after a cancelled cs-hide. Consumers listening to cs-show would see an event the user never triggered.
The new test does not settle the initial show animation before cancelling and hiding, unlike its siblings, so the final hide() can finish on the show animation's cancel event.
`expect(body.hidden).to.be.false` passes with or without the fix, and the test does not check the reflected `open` attribute or that cs-after-hide never fires.
